hub.title: Dog Breeds and Cat Breeds: Sizes, Temperament and Origins
hub.description: {dogs} dog breeds and {cats} cat breeds with size, weight, life expectancy, country of origin, FCI group, temperament and care, each with a photo and sources.
hub.lede: The most-read dog and cat breeds, one page each: where the breed comes from, how big it gets, its coat and temperament as kennel and cat clubs describe it, and what caring for one involves.
hub.sizeRule: Size groups come from the largest height (dogs) or weight (cats) Wikidata lists for the breed. Dogs: small under 41 cm at the withers, medium to 57 cm, large to 70 cm, giant above (by weight where no height is listed: under 10 kg, to 25 kg, to 45 kg, above). Cats: small under 5 kg, medium to 7 kg, large above.
about: Facts such as country of origin, height, weight, life expectancy and the FCI group come from Wikidata (CC0) and the Fédération Cynologique Internationale's breed list; a value Wikidata does not list is shown as a dash, never estimated. The text on each page summarises the breed's English Wikipedia article and the breed standards it links, and every page lists its sources.

Photos are freely licensed files from Wikimedia Commons, credited under each picture. Breeds were chosen by how often their Wikipedia articles are read in the site's eight languages. Health notes say only what sources commonly report; they are not veterinary advice.

faq.q: How many breeds are on cv.cm?
faq.a: {dogs} dog breeds and {cats} cat breeds, chosen by how often their Wikipedia articles were read in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Indonesian and Spanish over the past year.

The Fédération Cynologique Internationale sorts the breeds it recognises into ten groups by type and original work, from sheepdogs (group 1) to sighthounds (group 10). Some popular breeds, such as the American Pit Bull Terrier, are not recognised by the FCI.

faq.q: Where do the sizes and lifespans come from?
faq.a: From Wikidata, the free knowledge base behind Wikipedia. Where Wikidata has no figure the page shows a dash; the written overview may quote the range the breed standard or Wikipedia gives.
